label: Mastodon
terms_note: Free, per instance: register an app (POST /api/v1/apps) on the user's server → OAuth 2.0 authorization code with scopes write:statuses, write:media, read:statuses, read:notifications; default limits 300 requests per 5 min per account / IP, POST /api/v1/media 30 per 30 min, DELETE statuses 30 per 30 min (headers X-RateLimit-Limit / Remaining / Reset; instances may change them); instance rules on automation / bots (mark the account as a bot) apply; 500-character default limit varies by server.

tools.name: publish_video
tools.endpoint: same (v2 media accepts video; 202 while processing)

tools.name: analytics_account
tools.endpoint: — (followers_count on the Account entity; no insights API)

auth: 1. Register an app on the user's instance: `POST /api/v1/apps` {client_name, redirect_uris, scopes, website} →
2. OAuth 2.0 authorization code → `POST /oauth/token`; scopes `read:statuses read:notifications read:search
3. Mark the account as a **bot** when it is automated (`PATCH /api/v1/accounts/update_credentials {bot: true}`).

endpoints.call: POST /api/v1/statuses` {status, media_ids[], poll{options, expires_in}, in_reply_to_id, sensitive, spoiler_text, visibility public
POST /api/v2/media` (file, description, focus) → poll `GET /api/v1/media/:id` until processed

reference.limits: - Defaults: 300 requests / 5 min per account or IP; `POST /api/v1/media` 30 / 30 min; `DELETE` statuses 30 / 30 min (headers `X-RateLimit-Limit / Remaining / Reset`); instances may override. - Each instance's rules govern automation (bot flag, no unsolicited mentions, link posts often unlisted); links nofollow.

fields.name: token
fields.help: Mastodon user access token from the account's instance (Preferences > Development > New application, or an OAuth flow) with scopes read:accounts read:statuses read:notifications write:statuses; sent as `Authorization: Bearer`.

config_fields.name: instance
config_fields.help: Host of the account's Mastodon instance without scheme, e.g. mastodon.social; every call goes to https://<instance>/api/v1/...

me.note: GET /api/v1/accounts/verify_credentials (user token, read:accounts) returns the CredentialAccount {id, username, acct, display_name, url, followers_count, ...}.

publish_text.note: POST /api/v1/statuses {status, in_reply_to_id} (write:statuses) returns the Status {id, uri, url, created_at, content, account}. Visibility, language, spoiler_text and scheduled_at keep the instance defaults; the Idempotency-Key header is not sent.

read_comments.note: GET /api/v1/statuses/:id/context returns {ancestors, descendants}; every descendant Status (HTML `content`) is returned in one response, so page/limit are not sent.

reply_comment.note: A reply is a status with in_reply_to_id set to the comment's status id.

read_mentions.note: GET /api/v1/notifications?types[]=mention (read:notifications); limit defaults to 40, max 80. Mastodon paginates with Link headers / max_id, so `page` is not sent: pass `since` (a notification id, sent as since_id) to read newer mentions. `text` is the mentioning status's HTML content.

analytics_post.note: GET /api/v1/statuses/:id returns the Status with replies_count, reblogs_count and favourites_count (https://docs.joinmastodon.org/entities/Status/); the runtime cannot compose a nested `metrics` object, so counts are top-level fields.

delete.note: DELETE /api/v1/statuses/:id ('Delete one of your own statuses'; user token with write:statuses) returns 200 with the deleted Status carrying the source `text` (and poll / media_attachments) 'for reposting' - it is available under raw, and the runtime answers {status: 'deleted'}. 401 'The access token is invalid' is an auth_error; 404 'Status is not owned by you or does not exist' is an invalid_input. DELETE statuses is rate limited at 30 per 30 minutes (https://docs.joinmastodon.org/api/rate-limits/).

not_offered.publish_image: Images must first be uploaded as multipart files to POST /api/v2/media (then media_ids[] on the status); the runtime has no file upload.

evidence: host mastodon.social: DNS ok, TLSv1.3 (Let's Encrypt)
probe: 7/7 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 7/7 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; every parameter and body key named on the page
